blocks.x: I had a trumpet player who could play who could play very good. I'm trying to think, Willy Moore? I believe. I used to turn it over to him, you know, cause if they could handle it better than me, I would let them have it. You know? So, Dizzy could raise (inaudible). Clifford Brown. Did you call his playing beebop?
Cause he and Dizzy used to jam a lot. They used to jam a lot together.
Yeah, I'm almost sure cause they're coming out of that tradition. You
know, hard bob, or however they want to call it.
Yeah. But, he was, he was beautiful. Clifford and Dizzy.
He was such a melodic player, too. But, he's hard to classify just in that way.

Cause he did so much so early, Very eclectic (inaudible). He's sort of like Bach and Handel did at the end of the growth period, just sort of brought it together and culminated it. And, after that, you know, as you go into other directions but there isn't too much to do. So, he was sort of like, I would imagine, one of those that just sort of drew that whole, what is it, horizontal aspect of (inaudible) and leading into the lineal thing that was going to come.
But, he was of influence. I didn't get a chance to hear him too often. Like every now and then, I'd put a tape on by him. Over there, I have, I only have but one tape. I just happened to
find that downtown somewhere right off of Broadway. I think it was at Capital, one of those places.
And, every now and then, I like to, I like to listen at it cause he really, I really liked him.
